data.name: Yajurved
data.gender_notes: Yajurved is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Yajurved refers to the Vedas, a collection of sacred texts in Hinduism and Jainism. These texts are considered authoritative and contain rituals, mantras, and wisdom for spiritual growth. Yajurved is derived from the Sanskrit words yajus (sacred recitation) and veda (knowledge). The name Yajurved carries the meaning “Sacred recitation of Vedas” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Yajurved usually hope their child will grow to embody sacred recitation of vedas and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Yajurved belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sacred recitation of Vedas.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Yajurved total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The Yajurved is an essential part of the rich cultural heritage of India and Hinduism. It lays out the framework for various religious rituals and practices that have been passed down through generations. These rituals not only bring people closer to their faith and gods but also serve as markers of cultural identity for Hindus.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, the Yajurved is considered a divine source of knowledge, containing verses to connect individuals with the divine consciousness. It provides guidance on living a virtuous life and achieving spiritual enlightenment through meditation, self-discipline, and study of the scriptures. It is believed that reciting the verses from the Yajurved can purify the mind, body, and soul.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The Yajurved signifies the knowledge of yajnas (sacred rituals) and the recitation of hymns from the Yajurveda, which is believed to establish a connection between the devotee and the divine. It represents the path of action (karma marga) in Hindu spirituality.

vedic_reference.note: Yajurveda is one of the four Vedas, consisting of the Black and White Yajurveda. It contains mantras and rituals for daily life and religious ceremonies. The Yajurveda Samhita is the oldest known text of this Veda.

historical_references.reference: The Yajurveda is one of the four Vedas in Hinduism, and it is primarily concerned with the rituals, prayers, and formulas to be used by the Brahmin priests during various sacrifices and rituals. It is considered to be the practical application of the Rigveda and the Samaveda.
historical_references.context: The Yajurveda is believed to have been compiled during the late Vedic period.

historical_references.reference: The Yajurveda contains two major recensions: the Shukla Yajurveda and the Krishna Yajurveda. These recensions differ in their phonetic pronunciation and in certain rituals, but share a common textual basis.
historical_references.context: The divergent recensions of the Yajurveda reflect the geographical and cultural diversity of the Vedic civilization.
